summary: Listed as an unconfirmed lookout site, but the sources describe a hiking overlook on the Appalachian Trail and mention no tower.

access.note: Reached on foot along the Appalachian Trail from an access parking lot on VA-311 at the top of Catawba Mountain.

visit.trail_note: Wikipedia gives a climb of about 1,700 feet over about 4.7 miles from the VA-311 parking area.

evidence.supports: Association list: McAfee Knob, Roanoke County, unconfirmed, type and status unknown
The entry sits under the Unconfirmed Sites heading
McAfee Knob is a geological feature on Catawba Mountain, about 15 miles northwest of downtown Roanoke
evidence.quote: McAfee Knob is a geological feature with an elevation of 3,197 feet (974 m) above sea level, located on Catawba Mountain in Catawba, Virginia , roughly 15 miles northwest of Downtown Roanoke

evidence.supports: The view looks down about 1,600 feet to the Catawba Valley
evidence.quote: the vista offers panoramic views of the Catawba Valley, 1,600 feet (490 m) below

evidence.supports: The knob is named for James McAfee, a settler in the late 1730s
evidence.quote: McAfee Knob is named after James McAfee (Mac-a-fee), a Scottish-Irish immigrant who settled in the Catawba Valley in the late 1730s.

evidence.supports: The route passes an old fire road near a high-voltage power line clearing
evidence.quote: Remain on the trail and there will be an old fire road near a high voltage power line clearing.

evidence.supports: Much of Catawba Mountain was open farmland in the mid-1900s
evidence.quote: Much of Catawba Mountain was open farmland in the mid-1900s.

evidence.supports: Hiking to the knob began around the turn of the century, and parking was already an issue
evidence.quote: Folks began hiking to the knob around the turn of the century and even then there were issues with parking.

evidence.supports: The McAfee Knob trail is along the Appalachian Trail, managed by the Appalachian Trail Conservancy
evidence.quote: The McAfee Knob hiking trail is along the Appalachian Trail and is managed by the Appalachian Trail Conservancy.

evidence.supports: The hike from the VA-311 parking area is about 4.7 miles
evidence.quote: The hike is a climb of around 1,700 feet (520 m) and about 4.7 miles (7.6 km) to the top of the Knob from the VA-311 parking area.

evidence.supports: The trail starts from an access parking lot at the top of Catawba Mountain
evidence.quote: A.T. access parking lot on left at top of Catawba Mountain

evidence.supports: Wikipedia gives a four-mile northbound hike from VA-311
evidence.quote: a four-mile hike northbound from the intersection with VA-311 in Catawba, Virginia

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Wikipedia gives a four-mile northbound hike from the VA-311 intersection in one place and about 4.7 miles from the VA-311 parking area in another. The story uses the 4.7-mile figure.

notes_for_editor: The only source that calls McAfee Knob a lookout site is the association's Unconfirmed Sites list, which gives no type or status. Wikipedia calls the knob a geological feature and the trail-history article mentions no tower. A search result for a WDBJ7 news item about a brush fire near the summit appeared; I did not read it and it is undated, so it is not used. Consider reclassifying or hiding this record after review.
